text:
The Week Ahead: Currency Exchange Markets Cautious As Trump And Putin Meet The Week Ahead: Currency Exchange Markets Cautious As Trump And Putin Meet Facebook President Trump is meeting the Russian leader in Helsinki and markets are flat after a bullish week last week.
Scheduled events are light in the US, but the UK inflation report will be important for the upcoming BoE rate announcement.
Earnings season in the US continues, with some big Tech names reporting.
In terms of price action, there is not much to report about Monday’s session. Currency crosses are mostly flat, with EURGBP gaining just 0.02%. This kind of slow, range-bound action has persisted for most of the summer, if not year, in many crosses as drivers are thin on the ground and central bank policy changes at a snail’s pace. Dollar pairs are more lively, with EURUSD 0.26% higher as its oversold bounce continues. Retail sales in the US came in at +0.5%, slightly higher than the 0.4% expected, but down on the 1.3% reported in June.
Over the weekend, we saw Trump change his position on the UK trade deal, withdrawing his criticisms of Friday. There was some action from Special Prosecutor Mueller late on Friday, charging Russian intelligence officers with hacking the Clinton campaign in 2016, potentially handing the election to Trump. However, none of these events seemed to have much effect on trading early this week, and attention is perhaps on the big meeting in Helsinki as President Trump meets Russian President Putin. Trump will undoubtedly speak to the press, and traders will be watching for a softening position on sanctions, and any comments about oil production. This would affect Oil and RUB.
The rest of the week has some important scheduled events, as listed below, with the highlight probably being the UK inflation report as it could decide whether the BoE will either raise rates in August or stay put.
Tuesday July 17
In the UK, BoE Carney and Deputy Gov Cunliffe speak at 08:00 to Parliament about the Financial Stability Report, followed shortly by the nearest thing the UK has to NFP. New jobs are not actually reported, but all the other stats are there, including the important Average Hourly Earnings. The disinflationary version of this (AHE-CPI) is used by central banks to determine whether the public can afford rate hikes on their mortgages.
At 14:00, we have first day of Fed Chair Powell’s semi-annual Monetary Policy Report to Congress, known as the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, after the senators who introduced the bill that mandates the report.
Wednesday July 18
Attention moves to Europe with the British inflation figure following hot on the heels of the jobs report. These are the figures which will determine the UK rate decision on Aug 2. The second day of Humphrey-Hawkins (at 14:00) is usually less dramatic.
Thursday July 19
The Australian jobs report estimate is 40% higher than last month, and a beat may provide a boost for beleaguered AUD, which bounced off a 17-month low last week. The estimate of 17k is equivalent to 229k in the US which has 13.5x the population. The UK Retail Sales figure will add to the rate decision picture, although less so as it is only a proxy for CPI, released the day before. Fed Quarles (centrist, voter) speaks at 13:00. NDX giant MSFT (9.6% of the index, second only to AAPL and AMZN) reports after the bell.
Friday July 20
The week ends with OpEx day, the expiry of monthly options, which can cause of course heighten volatility. Fed Bullard (dove, non-voter) speaks at 12:00, and GE reports before the bell, the first earnings release since they left the DJIA after a 111-year run. The Canadian CPI estimate is slightly ahead of last month, but still below the May figure, as Canada still struggles to get traction in this area. As a rate hike already happened last week, it is difficult to foresee any CAD upside on this print. Advertisement
